title: Project Controls Manager (Data Center Construction)
description:
Who We Are:
Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.
The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.
What We Value:
We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.
Who You Are
You're a seasoned project controls professional with 7+ years managing schedule, cost, change, and documentation on large-scale, mission-critical construction programs — ideally in data centers, schedule-driven sector where downtime isn't an option. You read a P6 schedule critically — spotting broken logic, float that's been quietly manipulated, and a critical path that's about to move before it shows up in next week's update. You can pick apart a change order line by line and know a GMP well enough to catch a buyout gap before it becomes a claim.
You're equally comfortable pushing back on a general contractor in a weekly OAC meeting and briefing an executive on cost and schedule risk in five minutes flat. You don't wait to be asked for bad news — you surface it early, with the data to back it up. You build trust with GCs, design consultants, finance, and leadership not by being agreeable, but by being fair, prepared, and unwilling to accept a story that doesn't add up.
You think in systems — cost, schedule, risk, and change aren't separate disciplines to you, they're one integrated view of program health — and you're comfortable operating in an environment where the schedule compresses, the scope shifts, and the stakes don't.
What You'll Do

Manage the third-party scheduling consultants who review, analyze, and maintain the master schedule, setting expectations for quality, cadence, and reporting
Work directly with general contractors to review and validate their schedules — testing logic, durations, critical path, float, and sequencing against owner milestones
Own schedule health reporting to leadership, giving a clear, honest picture of progress, risk, and forecast, and escalating issues before they become delays
Own the change order process end-to-end: intake, review, verification, negotiation, and resolution
Critically evaluate change orders for scope, pricing, and schedule impact — verifying quantities, labor, markups, and backup rather than taking submissions at face value
Negotiate change orders directly with the general contractor to protect Galaxy's cost and schedule position
Represent Galaxy in weekly change and progress meetings with the GC, driving accountability and timely closure of open items
Maintain a complete, auditable change order log reconciled against the project budget and GMP
Serve as the bridge between field/GC reality and Finance's cost picture, ensuring both tell the same story
Own documentation control for active projects — RFIs, submittals, change documentation, meeting records, and contractual correspondence
Establish and improve project controls standards, templates, reporting, and governance across the portfolio

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience
7+ years of project controls or construction management experience on large-scale, complex programs; mission-critical or data center experience required
Proven experience managing schedule on the owner's side, including oversight of scheduling consultants and review of GC-maintained schedules
Deep, hands-on command of CPM scheduling and Primavera P6 — enough to interrogate a schedule, not just read one
Demonstrated experience owning the change order process, including verification and direct negotiation with general contractors
Strong working knowledge of construction contracts and GMP structures (AIA A133/A201 or similar)
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents
Excellent negotiation and communication skills, with the ability to hold GCs accountable and brief executives with equal credibility
Ability to manage controls across multiple concurrent projects in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

What You Bring

An owner's mindset — you protect the schedule, the GMP, and the record as if the capital were your own, and you hold contractors and consultants to that same standard.
The credibility to sit across from a general contractor and negotiate change with confidence, and the judgment to know which battles matter.
A sharp, detail-driven eye that catches the number that doesn't hold up, the logic that doesn't sequence, and the risk before it becomes a delay.
The versatility to move fluidly between the field, the GC, Finance, and the executive table, tailoring the message to each without losing the thread.
A bias for order and structure — you bring discipline to controls, documentation, and reporting in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
Willingness to travel up to 20% to Data Center sites as the work requires.

What We Offer:

Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
Flexible Time Off (i.e. unlimited paid vacation days)
Company paid Holidays (14)
Company paid sick leave
Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
3% 401(k) company contribution
Generous paid Parental Leave
Free virtual coaching and counseling sessions through Ginger
Free daily snacks in-office
Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.
Apply now and join us on our mission to engineer a new economic paradigm.Galaxy respects diversity and seeks to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and job applicants for employment without regard to actual or perceived age, race, color, creed, religion, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), gender identity or gender expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital or partnership or caregiver status, ancestry, national origin, citizenship status, disability, military or veteran status, protected medical condition as defined by applicable state or local law, genetic information or predisposing genetic characteristic, or other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.
We will endeavor to make a reasonable accommodation to the known limitations of a qualified applicant with a disability unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business. If you believe you require such assistance to complete the application process or to participate in an interview, please contact careers@galaxy.com.

title: Foreman
description:
Job Title: Foreman 
Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro South  Location: Afton, TX / On-site Reports to: Site Superintendent Employment Type: Full-Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt 
About Loenbro 
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation. 
Position Summary
The Foreman is responsible for overseeing and coordinating daily pipeline construction, installation, maintenance, and repair activities. This role provides direct supervision to field crews, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and in compliance with company standards, client requirements, and regulatory guidelines. The Pipeline Foreman serves as the primary field leader and acts as the key liaison between craft personnel, subcontractors, and project management.
Essential Responsibilities

Supervise and direct pipeline construction crews in the installation, maintenance, and repair of pipeline systems.
Plan and coordinate daily work activities, manpower, equipment, and material requirements.
Review project drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and construction schedules.
Conduct daily safety meetings and enforce all company, client, and regulatory safety requirements.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, DOT, environmental, and company policies.
Coordinate excavation, trenching, pipe installation, welding, coating, hydrostatic testing, tie-ins, and restoration activities.
Verify elevations, grades, alignments, and installation requirements are met according to project specifications.
Monitor crew productivity, project progress, and quality standards.
Identify and resolve field issues that could impact project schedules or budgets.
Coordinate with inspectors, utility companies, landowners, subcontractors, and project stakeholders.
Maintain accurate daily reports, production records, timesheets, equipment utilization reports, and safety documentation.
Ensure proper use, maintenance, and accountability of company equipment and tools.
Train and mentor crew members, fostering a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
Assist project management with project planning, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Participate in incident investigations and implement corrective actions when necessary.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED.
5+ years of pipeline construction experience.
2+ years of supervisory or foreman experience leading pipeline crews.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction methods, excavation, trench safety, and utility coordination.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and survey information.
Knowledge of OSHA regulations and industry safety standards.
Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to pass pre-employment and client-required screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with oil & gas, natural gas, water, wastewater, or industrial pipeline projects.
OSHA 30 Certification.
NCCER Foreman Certification.
First Aid/CPR Certification.
Competent Person Trenching and Excavation Certification.
Experience managing subcontractors and multiple work crews.
Knowledge of hydrostatic testing, welding inspection processes, and pipeline integrity requirements.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong leadership and team management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction equipment and methods.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Ability to work effectively with project managers, superintendents, inspectors, clients, and field personnel.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Frequent standing, walking, bending, kneeling, climbing, and lifting up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and travel as project demands require.
Ability to safely access active construction sites and uneven terrain.

Work Environment

Heavy civil and pipeline construction projects.
Exposure to construction equipment, noise, dust, vibration, and changing weather conditions.
Travel between project locations may be required.

Benefits 
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team: 

Medical, dental, and vision insurance 

401(k) retirement plan with company match 

Paid time off (PTO) 

Life and disability insurance 

Professional development and training opportunities 

Employee assistance program (EAP) 

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked. 
 
Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities.  If you’re ready to be part of a company that LEADS by: 

Living with Integrity 

Exceeding Expectations 

Acting with Urgency 

Delivering Excellence 

 
…we want to hear from you. 
 
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

 Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro - South Location: Afton, TX Reports To: Superintendent Employment Type: Full Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Position Overview: Loenbro Industrial Services Group is seeking to hire experienced Millwrights for our North Dakota jobsite.
As a Millwright, you will install, assemble, dismantle, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair machinery to specifications. Millwrights use precision tools and processes to ensure that the machinery is installed and working correctly and ensuring compliance with all safety regulations and guidelines. We offer a competitive salary, a full range of benefits, a challenging work environment, and growth potential.
Job Duties:

Work with industry-specific and complex precision machines, including but not limited to exhaust fans, generators, hydraulic systems, pumps, gears, bearings, compressors, etc.
Plan, inspect, verify, and document the scope of work.
Use precision leveling and alignment tools to measure angles, material thickness, and small distances with calipers, squares, micrometers, optical instruments, and other tools.
Fit bearings, align gears and wheels, attach motors, and connect belts according to manufacturer’s blueprints and drawings.
Dismantle machines using hammers, wrenches, crowbars, and other hand tools.
Assemble and install equipment such as shafting, exhaust fan blades, and pump systems.
Assemble machines and bolt, weld, rivet, and fasten machinery to foundations or other structures using hand tools and power tools.
Operate engine lathes, grinders, and files.
May construct foundations for machinery.
Fabricate and install parts, equipment, and machinery by measuring, cutting, drilling, and/or welding.
Unload, inspect, move, and set equipment into position using cranes, hoists, dollies, rollers, and trucks.
Use rigging and hoisting devices such as chokers, chain falls, and come-alongs to move equipment/materials into place.
Conduct preventative maintenance such as lubrication and fixing or repairing worn parts.
Follow directions from the supervisor.
Must be willing to perform other duties as assigned.
Other duties as assigned.
Able to recognize changing ground conditions.
Adheres to all safety rules.
Maintaining the work areas in a clean, safe, and orderly manner on a continuous basis
Perform all other job duties as assigned.

Skill/Qualifications:

Must have experience with industrial machinery installation, repair, and maintenance.
Must know how to read blueprints, schematic drawings, and engineering specifications, and understand how to read and interpret technical manuals to determine work procedures.
Must have experience using industrial hand tools and power tools.
Must have all Journeyman Precision Millwright hand tools.
Minimum 4-5 years of industrial construction/maintenance experience.
Minimum of 3 years of Millwright experience.
Must have reliable transportation.

Essential Requirements:

Demonstrated industrial construction/maintenance history experience.
Knowledge of hand tools, power tools, and layout tools such as lasers, ultrasonic measuring and alignment tools, plumb bobs, cutting torches, welding machines, hydraulic torch wrenches, hydraulic stud tensioners, soldering guns, and metalworking equipment, including lathes and grinding machines.
Organization and time management.
Good problem-solving abilities.
Good aptitude and manual dexterity
Knowledge of math concepts, geometry, and layout.
Demonstrated ability to lead others and provide detailed instructions.
Ability to work with others – team player.
Ability to work independently – minimal supervision.
Effective communication skills with co-workers and supervisors.
Employees are required to adhere to large amounts of standing, walking, bending, squatting, and lifting.
Employees may be required to lift, carry, and move up to 50 lbs.
Will occasionally work at heights, climb ladders and stairways, and work off platforms.
Must be capable of working outside in the elements, including, but not limited to heat, cold, rain, snow, and wind; and must be able to work for prolonged periods, up to 12 hours a day.
Employees will be required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) i.e. hard hat, safety glasses/goggles, ear plugs/muffs, masks/respirators, safety vests, gloves, and steel-toe boots.
Walking on uneven terrain, with an average of two miles per day.
Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors
If driving is required, a valid driver’s license and proof of insurability will be required. All drivers are subject to a DMV background records search. 

 
This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S) policies.
Benefits
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Paid time off (PTO)
Life and disability insurance
Professional development and training opportunities
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.
Our Core Values (LEAD)
At Loenbro, we are guided by our core values:

Living with Integrity
Exceeding Expectations
Acting with Urgency
Delivering Excellence

If you're ready to join a company committed to building exceptional projects, developing outstanding people, and delivering excellence every day, we want to hear from you.
Equal Opportunity Employer
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Job Title: QA/QC Manager
Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro - South       Location: Andrews, TX / On-site Reports to: Job Superintendent Employment Type: Full-Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt 
About Loenbro 
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation. 
The Industrial QA/QC Inspector is responsible for ensuring that construction, fabrication, installation, and maintenance activities comply with project specifications, quality standards, industry codes, and client requirements. This role performs inspections, audits, testing, and documentation reviews to verify that work is completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved quality control procedures. The Industrial QA/QC Inspector works closely with project management, field personnel, subcontractors, and clients to maintain quality excellence throughout all phases of the project.
Essential Responsibilities

Perform quality assurance and quality control inspections on industrial construction and maintenance projects.
Verify compliance with project specifications, drawings, codes, standards, and client requirements.
Conduct inspections of materials, equipment, fabrication, installation, and completed work.
Review construction documents, inspection test plans (ITPs), quality procedures, and work packages.
Verify proper implementation of approved procedures, work instructions, and quality programs.
Document inspection findings and prepare detailed quality reports.
Coordinate and witness testing activities, including pressure testing, hydrostatic testing, and functional testing as required.
Inspect structural steel, piping systems, mechanical installations, coatings, and electrical installations based on project scope.
Identify non-conforming work and issue deficiency reports when required.
Track corrective actions and verify resolution of quality issues.
Coordinate inspections with clients, third-party inspectors, and regulatory agencies.
Maintain quality records, turnover packages, test reports, material certifications, and inspection documentation.
Support project audits and quality reviews.
Participate in project meetings and communicate quality concerns to project leadership.
Promote continuous improvement initiatives related to quality and compliance.
Ensure all activities are performed in accordance with company safety policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED required.
Associate degree or technical training in Construction Management, Engineering Technology, Welding Technology, or a related field preferred.
3+ years of experience in quality control, quality assurance, inspection, construction, fabrication, or industrial maintenance.
Working knowledge of construction codes, standards, and inspection processes.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, P&IDs, isometric drawings, and quality documents.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and construction documentation systems.
Strong organizational, communication, and report-writing skills.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to pass required pre-employment and client-specific screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification.
NACE/AMPP Coating Inspector certification.
API certifications applicable to project scope.
ASNT Level II certification in NDT methods.
OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.
Experience in power generation, oil & gas, utility, manufacturing, mining, or industrial construction environments.
Experience with mechanical, piping, structural, electrical, or coatings inspections.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Thorough understanding of QA/QC principles and industry best practices.
Ability to interpret drawings, specifications, inspection procedures, and quality requirements.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to identify quality deficiencies and recommend corrective actions.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently while maintaining strong collaboration with project teams.
Strong documentation and record management skills.
Commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

Physical Requirements

Ability to walk active construction and industrial job sites for extended periods.
Ability to climb ladders, access elevated work areas, and navigate uneven terrain.
Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather and environmental conditions.
Ability to travel between project locations as required.

Work Environment

Industrial facilities, manufacturing plants, power generation facilities, utility projects, fabrication shops, and construction sites.
Exposure to noise, dust, heavy equipment, welding operations, elevated work areas, and changing weather conditions.
Work may require access to confined spaces, elevated structures, and active construction zones.

The Industrial QA/QC Inspector is responsible for ensuring that construction, fabrication, installation, and maintenance activities comply with project specifications, quality standards, industry codes, and client requirements. This role performs inspections, audits, testing, and documentation reviews to verify that work is completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved quality control procedures. The Industrial QA/QC Inspector works closely with project management, field personnel, subcontractors, and clients to maintain quality excellence throughout all phases of the project.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Perform quality assurance and quality control inspections on industrial construction and maintenance projects.
  • Verify compliance with project specifications, drawings, codes, standards, and client requirements.
  • Conduct inspections of materials, equipment, fabrication, installation, and completed work.
  • Review construction documents, inspection test plans (ITPs), quality procedures, and work packages.
  • Verify proper implementation of approved procedures, work instructions, and quality programs.
  • Document inspection findings and prepare detailed quality reports.
  • Coordinate and witness testing activities, including pressure testing, hydrostatic testing, and functional testing as required.
  • Inspect structural steel, piping systems, mechanical installations, coatings, and electrical installations based on project scope.
  • Identify non-conforming work and issue deficiency reports when required.
  • Track corrective actions and verify resolution of quality issues.
  • Coordinate inspections with clients, third-party inspectors, and regulatory agencies.
  • Maintain quality records, turnover packages, test reports, material certifications, and inspection documentation.
  • Support project audits and quality reviews.
  • Participate in project meetings and communicate quality concerns to project leadership.
  • Promote continuous improvement initiatives related to quality and compliance.
  • Ensure all activities are performed in accordance with company safety policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Associate degree or technical training in Construction Management, Engineering Technology, Welding Technology, or a related field preferred.
  • 3+ years of experience in quality control, quality assurance, inspection, construction, fabrication, or industrial maintenance.
  • Working knowledge of construction codes, standards, and inspection processes.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, P&IDs, isometric drawings, and quality documents.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and construction documentation systems.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and report-writing skills.
  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to pass required pre-employment and client-specific screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

  • AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification.
  • NACE/AMPP Coating Inspector certification.
  • API certifications applicable to project scope.
  • ASNT Level II certification in NDT methods.
  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.
  • Experience in power generation, oil & gas, utility, manufacturing, mining, or industrial construction environments.
  • Experience with mechanical, piping, structural, electrical, or coatings inspections.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Thorough understanding of QA/QC principles and industry best practices.
  • Ability to interpret drawings, specifications, inspection procedures, and quality requirements.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to identify quality deficiencies and recommend corrective actions.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining strong collaboration with project teams.
  • Strong documentation and record management skills.
  • Commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to walk active construction and industrial job sites for extended periods.
  • Ability to climb ladders, access elevated work areas, and navigate uneven terrain.
  • Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather and environmental conditions.
  • Ability to travel between project locations as required.

Work Environment

  • Industrial facilities, manufacturing plants, power generation facilities, utility projects, fabrication shops, and construction sites.
  • Exposure to noise, dust, heavy equipment, welding operations, elevated work areas, and changing weather conditions.
  • Work may require access to confined spaces, elevated structures, and active construction zones.

Company Description

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.Job Description
As an FTTx Designer, you will be responsible for creating fiber-to-the-x (FTTx) designs. Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following: sizing of serving boundaries using GIS address data; analyze, interpret, and organize large datasets; determine feeder routes, distribution routes, and drops to premises by utilizing, parcel, ROW, and easement documentation; determine fiber allocations; reviewing field staking sheets, as-Builts and field collected data to determine the optimal running line and construction method. Analyze aerial Imagery and general maps to identify existing utilities or potential obstructions; and produce and review high-quality constructible plan sets using GIS based software.

Qualifications

You are passionate about:

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

You bring to the team:

Ability to read, interpret, create maps and plan sets.
Ability to edit and create PDF documents (Bluebeam or Adobe skills)
Associate’s/bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.
General knowledge in OSP construction methods and best practices.
3-6 years of FTTx design and/or OSP experience.
General knowledge of FTTx and/or OSP networks is required.
Knowledge of Google Earth KMZ files.
Knowledge of AutoCAD based software is preferred.
Knowledge of ESRI ArcGIS Software products is preferred.
Knowledge of asset management platforms is preferred ((IQGEO, NetDesigner, CrescentLink, etc.)

title: Construction Foreman
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.CONSTRUCTION FOREMAN
Starbase is expanding its site infrastructure to support ongoing operations and growth. As a Construction Foreman on the Starbase Infrastructure team, you will lead a crew of technicians, laborers, and contractors in the field to build, maintain, and improve industrial facilities, utilities, and civil infrastructure across the site. Work may include earthwork, concrete, carpentry, structural steel, mechanical, electrical, piping, plumbing, HVAC, and related site utilities.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Lead day-to-day field work for assigned infrastructure projects, including work assignments, crew productivity, quality, and schedule
Supervise and instruct technicians, laborers, and subcontractors; set daily priorities and resolve field conflicts
Read and interpret drawings, specifications, and survey control to lay out work and verify grades, elevations, and dimensions
Plan and sequence construction activities across a range of trades as assigned (earthwork, concrete, framing, MEP, finishes, and related civil/industrial work)
Coordinate material deliveries, staging, equipment, and tools so the crew can work without delay
Estimate labor, materials, and equipment needs for assigned scopes; requisition materials and maintain simple, accurate field records
Enforce SpaceX safety policies and jobsite cleanliness; stop work for unsafe conditions and ensure incident reporting procedures are followed
Perform and oversee hands-on construction work as needed
Use hand tools, power tools, and construction equipment; ensure tools and equipment are maintained and secured at the end of each shift
Coordinate with engineering, project management, and adjacent trades to keep work aligned with broader site goals
Maintain a daily log of crew activities, progress, issues, and manpower; report status to supervision as required
Adjust crew size, sequence, and methods as needed to meet deadlines and quality standards; escalate issues that affect cost, schedule, or design

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate 
2+ years of experience as a foreman or crew lead

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Experience leading crews in a general construction or multi-trade environment
Familiarity with common construction trades such as earthwork, concrete, carpentry, mechanical, electrical, piping, and site utilities
Knowledge of standard methods, materials, tools, and equipment used in industrial and civil construction
Ability to interpret blueprints, shop drawings, and specifications, and to make field calculations for areas, volumes, and material quantities
Ability to instruct and direct skilled, semi-skilled, and unskilled workers
Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety practices applicable to construction work
Experience in a fast-paced construction environment with changing priorities
Written and verbal communication skills; use of MS Outlook and Teams
Experience with heavy equipment, forklifts, boom lifts, and/or scissor lifts
Ability to offer field feedback to the design team to improve cost, quality, and constructibility

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Work hours depend on site priorities and may require extended hours, weekends, and holidays; flexibility required
Periodic work in extreme outdoor environments: heat, cold, wind, rain
Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. unassisted
Basic mechanical aptitude and ability to perform regular manual labor
Must be able to stand for long periods of time; work at heights, climbing up and down ladders, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, and stretching may be required
Ability to work in confined spaces as required by the work
Must have a valid driver’s license
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.  

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role

Crusoe is seeking a motivated Construction Project Specialist to support our growing portfolio of AI Factory

and Cloud Services colocation projects. This role is ideal for early-career construction professionals or

technically experienced candidates looking to expand their construction expertise in a fast-paced,

innovative environment. As a generalist, you'll support the planning, coordination, and execution of critical

infrastructure projects while developing experience across construction, mechanical and electrical systems, and data center deployment.

What You'll Do:

Assist in managing daily activities across active construction sites, including scheduling, site

coordination, documentation, and vendor oversight

Support senior Construction Managers with project tracking, contractor communications, RFI logs, andsubmittal reviews

Monitor construction progress and help identify risks, delays, or quality concerns, escalating to project leadership as needed

Interface with internal stakeholders (engineering, procurement, operations) and external partners (GCs, vendors, consultants)

Participate in project planning and due diligence meetings, supporting coordination across

construction, engineering, facilities, and operations teams

Review and analyze project schedules and support coordination of work across contractors, vendors, and internal stakeholdersParticipate in site walks, inspections, and punch-list generation

Support budgeting and cost tracking efforts, including reviewing invoices and change orders Help maintain accurate records, drawings, closeout documentation, and as-builts

Develop toward independently managing project activities and leading coordination meetings as experience and project knowledge grow

Ensure safety practices and site protocols are followed in accordance with Crusoe's standards Travel domestically and internationally as required to support project deployments.

What You Bring:

2-5 years of relevant experience in commercial construction, engineering, critical facilities, facilities operations, or a related technical environment

A solid foundation in commercial construction with some technical exposure, OR strong technical experience with exposure to construction/project delivery

Familiarity with core construction processes including scheduling, procurement, and documentation

Comfortable reading construction drawings and interpreting specifications

Experience working with or alongside general contractors, trade partners, vendors, or technical service providers

Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail

Proficiency with tools like Procore, Bluebeam, or similar construction management platforms

Strong communication skills and a proactive, solution-oriented mindset

Nice to Have:

Experience in data center, industrial, or mission-critical infrastructure environments

Experience with mechanical and/or electrical systems, whether gained through construction,

engineering, facilities operations, or another technical environment

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or related field, or

equivalent relevant technical/construction experience

Ability and willingness to obtain and maintain a valid passport for international project travel

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $110,000- 135,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

  • Experience with electrical safety standards (e.g., NFPA70E/OSHA30

  • Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective collaboration and reporting.

title: Apprentice Electrician
description:
Job Title: Apprentice Electrician  
Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/ Loenbro - South Reports to: General Superintendent  Employment Type: Full-Time FLSA Classification: N-Non-Exempt 
About Loenbro 
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication, and our vertical market focus spans all industries. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex, so that our clients gain clarity and control in construction and maintenance. We do this by taking full ownership on every interaction, delivering multi-scope project excellence, and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners as we enhance and maintain your critical infrastructure. We have a national presence but a local approach—so that every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. Through their relationship with us and the One Loenbro model, our customers are able to simplify, control, and succeed in the everyday. 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.  
Job Summary 
 
Loenbro is hiring a  Apprentice Electrician, under the direction of Journeyman Electricians, is responsible for the installation, start-up, troubleshooting, commissioning and servicing of industrial / commercial electrical equipment and systems. This position will be responsible for following the directions of the Journeyman Electrician to complete electrical maintenance and repair work.  
 
Essential Job Responsibilities  
 

Observe, learn, and understand a wide range of skills and processes under the instruction of a skilled electrician. 

Demonstrate these skills and processes as on-the-job training progresses by working independently or with others to complete assigned tasks. 

Learn and understand the importance of safety within the workspace and across projects 

Learn about the various tools and materials required for electricians to complete tasks and projects. 

Maintain good housekeeping and organization in the work area. 

Properly utilize the required tools and equipment for each specific task.

title: Construction Supervisor
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISOR
As a critical member of the Starbase Infrastructure team, you will supervise and lead a group of laborers and contractors to enable the build and activation of infrastructure for a variety of projects.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Oversee the day-to-day site supervision of a fast-paced, high impact construction project including the responsibilities below:

Supervise a team dedicated to construction site logistics/operations, including work schedules, project progress, and resource allocation
Plan, implement, and enforce construction site logistics to enable broader project goals and schedule
Manage SpaceX construction assets (trailers, portas, rental equipment, etc.)
Implement and enforce SpaceX safety policies. Drive the safety culture on the jobsite through contractor and internal partners
Daily field coordination and conflict resolution for contractors and internal partners
Manage site logistics, including daily deliveries, offloading, inventory, storage, and staging of SpaceX purchased materials
Responsible for jobsite cleanliness
Create, enforce, and iterate on schedules for workers and subcontractors in conjunction with engineering and project management team
Maintain a daily log for the job site’s operations, reporting to management as necessary

Oversee the procurement and execution of specific construction projects as delegated by the engineering & project management team

Provide budgetary costs based upon the preliminary scope of the project
Gather proposals from contractors; assign contracts upon receipt of all proposals
Develop the final cost and schedule for the sub-project, and implement controls as needed to manage cost, schedule and scope
Coordinate project implementation and track project status
Coordinate with end user and facilities team for building operations and maintenance
Supervise night shift contractors as project work requires

Make changes in the operation as necessary to best meet construction deadlines, triage issues to engineering & project management team as necessary to ensure schedule and quality are adequate

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
2+ years of professional experience in engineering, construction management, architecture or facilities management

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Field experience in a technical field or in supervising a multi-discipline team of contractors/laborers
Previous experience with project management and scheduling software
Understanding of multiple disciplines such as civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, piping, geotechnical, and surveying
Experience with project management of construction projects including estimating, cost control, schedule, and contractor management
Experience reading, reviewing, and approving shop and fabrication drawings
Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while maintaining a high sense of urgency in a high-paced, challenging work environment
Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Ability to work at elevated heights (200+ feet)
Physical effort with lifting and carrying materials or equipment (up to 25 lbs.)
Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain
Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise
Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on site operational needs; flexibility required
Valid driver’s license
Travel may be required based on specific project tasks
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Automation Construction Manager, NA
description:
About Vantage Data Centers


Vantage Data Centers powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Construction Department

The Construction team is responsible for the entire process flow of delivering the physical data centers from shovel ready state through commissioning, working with Sales, Operations, and management along the way. Construction implements and executes upon the work product developed by the Development & Engineering (D&E) team. The team also manages Vantage’s build partners to success through technical feedback and review, and actively participating in review of schedule, safety and budget. Many times, a role like this at other companies is purely oversight. One thing that distinguishes Vantage is that our construction teams are given the responsibility and authority to directly drive the process. When compared to external resources, our internal team can ensure the key stakeholders are engaged in the decision-making process to align long-term operational sustainability with value engineering and cost metrics to deliver products aligned with corporate goals. This approach empowers each member of the team to drive high- impact decisions and even more impactful results.

Position Overview

This role will be based on site at our Shackelford County, TX location. 

Vantage is seeking an experienced Automation Construction Manager to lead the planning, installation, integration, testing, and commissioning of automation and controls systems across mission critical data center projects.

This role will oversee the partners responsible of the construction and deployment of building automation systems (BAS), SCADA systems, HVAC controls, control panels, fan systems, valve controls, alarm monitoring systems, and environmental conditioning systems supporting data center operations. The Automation Construction Manager will coordinate with mechanical, electrical, controls, and commissioning teams to ensure automation infrastructure is installed, integrated and commissioned in accordance with project requirements.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise in industrial and facility automation with proven construction project management experience, including scheduling, contractor management, budgeting, risk mitigation, and stakeholder coordination.

Essential Job Functions

Manage project scope, schedule, budget, and execution for automation and controls-related construction activities.

Lead installation and integration of Building Management Systems (BMS), Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS), Building Automation Systems (BAS), SCADA platforms, PLC-based controls, and facility monitoring systems.

Coordinate automation requirements throughout design, procurement, construction, startup, commissioning, and turnover phases.

Oversee installation and functional testing of:

HVAC control systems

Variable frequency drives (VFDs)

Fan wall control systems

Chilled water and condenser water valve controls

Temperature and humidity monitoring systems

Alarm and notification systems

Environmental conditioning controls

High-temperature and low-flow operating sequences

Partner with Engineering, Operations, Commissioning, and Construction teams to ensure controls systems support facility reliability and operational requirements.

Drive automation system readiness for integrated systems testing (IST) and commissioning activities.

Lead general contractor and its associated controls contractors, automation vendors, and system integrators throughout project delivery along with internal Automation support stakeholder.

Review and validate automation sequences of operation, points lists, network architecture, and control drawings.

Develop and manage project schedules, critical path activities, and commissioning milestones.

Identify project risks and develop mitigation strategies to maintain schedule and operational objectives.

Duties

Coordinate automation and controls activities with MEP, CSA, commissioning, and operations teams.

Review automation design packages, control schematics, panel layouts, SCADA architecture, and network diagrams.

Manage construction and installation of control panels, field devices, instrumentation, sensors, actuators, and communication networks.

Oversee startup and commissioning of:

Air handling units (AHUs)

CRAHs and CRACs

Cooling towers

Chiller plants

Pump systems

Environmental control systems

Electrical LV systems

Electrical MV Systems

Whitespace distribution equipment

Monitor progress against project schedules and coordinate resolution of field conflicts.

Ensure controls systems comply with project specifications, design standards, operational requirements, and applicable codes.

Support integrated systems testing and troubleshooting of automation-related issues.

Review contractor invoices and validate field progress.

Manage vendor performance and coordinate corrective actions when required.

Maintain project reporting including forecasting, budgeting, risk logs, and schedule updates.

Develop lessons learned, value engineering and process improvements focused on controls and automation implementation.

Support operational turnover activities including documentation reviews, training coordination, and acceptance testing.

Additional responsibilities assigned bmy manager.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Industrial Automation, Controls Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience.

7+ years of experience managing automation, controls, industrial systems, HVAC controls, or mission critical construction projects.

Experience with Building Automation Systems (BAS), Building Management Systems (BMS), and SCADA platforms required.

Experience with automation control strategies supporting HVAC, cooling plants, environmental conditioning systems, and critical infrastructure.

Working knowledge of:

SCADA architecture

PLC systems

Industrial controls

HVAC controls

BACnet, Modbus, and industrial communication protocols

Alarm monitoring systems

Control panel fabrication and installation

Instrumentation and field devices

Experience managing controls contractors, system integrators, commissioning providers, and equipment vendors.

Strong understanding of commissioning processes, sequence of operations testing, and integrated systems testing.

Experience with mission critical facilities, data centers, pharmaceutical facilities, semiconductor plants, manufacturing facilities, power generation facilities, or industrial processing environments preferred.

Demonstrated project management expertise including scheduling, resource planning, budgeting, forecasting, risk mitigation, and stakeholder management.

Proficiency with Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or similar scheduling tools preferred.

Preferred Background

Data Center construction and commissioning experience.

Industrial automation, process controls, or facility controls background.

Hands-on experience with HVAC optimization, chilled water systems, airflow management, valve sequencing, and environmental monitoring systems.

Experience supporting large-scale mission critical facilities where system uptime, reliability, and operational resilience are key business requirements.

Physical Demands and Special Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle, or feel objects; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop or kneel; talk and hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

Additional Details

This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits.

Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including your qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience and may fall outside of the range shown.

#LI-Onsite #LI-CM2

We operate with No Ego and No Arrogance. We work to build each other up and support one another, appreciating each other’s strengths and respecting each other’s weaknesses. We find joy in our work and each other, actively seeking opportunities to inject fun into what we do. Our hard and efficient work is rewarded with an above market total compensation package. We offer a comprehensive suite of health and welfare, retirement, and paid leave benefits exceeding local expectations.


Throughout the year, the advantage of being part of the Vantage team is evident with an array of benefits, recognition, training and development, and the knowledge that your contribution adds value to the company and our community.

title: Senior BIM Designer MEP, Data Center Engineering
location: Austin, Texas, United States; Denver, Colorado, United States; Remote US; Seattle, Washington, United States
description:
Overview
Fleet Data Centers designs, builds and operates mega-scale data center campuses. Fleet provides its customers flexibility and predictability to meet their upside demand forecasts, addressing a key need in the market as traditional leased models are struggling to keep pace with the demand for new Cloud and AI infrastructure. Fleet is led by a team of industry veterans that have already made a lasting imprint on the evolution of global digital infrastructure and are committed and uniquely capable of upleveling data center development scale and operations in the face of rising demand. Fleet is well positioned to bring in-house design, engineering and operational capabilities to collaborate with customers on tailored solutions for campuses of 500MW+. This unique model enables Fleet to provide the world’s largest and most sophisticated customers a seamless extension of their own data center fleets with constant access to design innovation. Fleet is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with satellite offices in Seattle, WA and Arlington, VA.
 
Position Overview:
The Senior BIM Designer MEP Engineer will be responsible for reviewing project Revit and Navisworks models assessing model development, modeling standards and practices and adherence to the BIM standards and compile your comments on the same. They will be responsible for supporting partner teams such as design, construction, and operations.
 
The BIM Designer MEP will be responsible for establishing and maintaining BIM standards, processes, and workflows. The candidate shall also be responsible for the BIM lifecycle of multiple design projects across the globe.
The candidate shall also be responsible for developing piping, instrumentation, and electrical plantroom layouts along with single line diagrams and schematics.
 
Key Responsibilities:

BIM Implementation Strategy, establishing and maintaining BIM standards, processes, and workflows as well as educating and training internal teams in BIM software and procedures
BIM oversight of all aspects of the data center life cycle starting with design, construction, and maintenance of data center BIM models
Lead discussions in engineering and construction best practices, supporting the wider team by sharing knowledge with a view to establishing new standards
Develop BIM Implementation strategy and deliver complex international projects
Establish and ensure BIM files meet Fleet Data Center standards and are always following the BIM Guidelines during the project by reviewing consultant BIM documentation, BIM files, coordinate output formats, and validate data quality, collect design documents and files for projects
CDE Management, establish and administer the CDE and support efficient management of multi-stakeholder projects
Project Management, coordinating BIM execution and project delivery with project leadership
BIM Execution, create and maintain the project’s industry framework documents including BEP, MIDP, MPDT, appendices etc.
Technical support, establish data-integrated workflows for building projects and provide support, guidance and training to project teams
Digital technology and content management, oversee the production of smart object content, templates and libraries in the context of the project, deploy the use of Fleet Data Centers content management system Autodesk Content Catalog or other onto projects and manage the best practice use of digital technology for collaboration, coordination and delivery
Quality, establish and administer the digital quality assurance control procedures
Working with multiple design and engineering professionals on concepts and build projects

Required Qualifications:

Extensive experience in managing MEP delivery across multiple projects or business units
5+ years of design and construction experience
5+ years working with Revit
5+ years working with Navisworks
Strong technical knowledge of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems
Strong problem-solving, analytical and strategic planning skills
Excellent organization skills in archival and maintenance operations of project documents
Experience with Tier 1 contractor projects or complex multi-disciplinary programs
Familiarity with digital construction tools, BIM and lean methodologies
Extensive knowledge of software packages such as ACC and Procore
Experience in the establishment and management of BIM and VDC models including orientation, geo-positioning, co-ordination and the set-up of model reviews

Preferred Qualifications:

Degree or equivalent in mechanical, electrical, building services or related discipline
Experience in mission critical design
Experience in piping design and chilled water piping and instrumentation layout, plantroom layout design and electrical architecture
Professional accreditation or membership of a relevant body such as CIBSE, IET, Engineers Ireland
Postgraduate qualification in building services, project management or sustainability
Training in digital design, BIM management or innovative MEP technologies

Key Competencies:

Integrity and Ethical Standards: Build trust, ensure fairness, and foster long-term, transparent relationships with suppliers
Effective Communication: The ability to clearly convey expectations and requirements to suppliers and negotiation parties, while understanding their needs and concerns. Comfortable delivering written and verbal presentations to internal leadership teams
Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Ability to understand the emotions, cultural nuances, and motivations of others, while effectively managing one's own emotions during high-pressure negotiations
Strategic Thinking: Ability to think big picture while also managing granular details
Adaptability: Proven track record of managing change and ambiguity in a fast-paced environment
Leadership: Ability to manage cross-functional teams and external vendors
Experience with complex, multi-site projects: Manage multiple projects under tight deadlines and deliver exceptional results
Excellent communication and presentation skills: Capable of interfacing with senior leadership and diverse stakeholders
Creative problem-solver: Ability to troubleshoot and optimize system performance effectively

Working Conditions:

This role requires occasional travel to data center sites across multiple regions (up to 25% travel)
Ability to work in both office environments and active construction sites, adhering to all safety protocols

 
Expected Salary Range: $120,000 - $150,000 Salary + Discretionary Bonus
 
Seattle, WA (Mercer Island), Denver, CO, or Alexandria, VAA.
Fleet Data Centers Employment
Fleet Data Centers employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO. 
 
NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the organization's ongoing needs.
 
Fleet Data Centers is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants are considered for employment regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or veteran status. If you need assistance applying for any of our open positions, please contact us at info@fleetdatacenters.com.

title: Sr Estimator (Heavy Civil)
description:
At Keeley Companies, we believe in empowering our people and fulfilling career aspirations. Keeley is a career destination with countless opportunities for advancement, and a world-class family culture that is centered around creating the best possible environment for our people to thrive.Keeley Construction is looking to hire a Sr Estimator for our Heavy Civil Group in New Braunfels, TX.
Primary Responsibilities

Provide leadership for estimates and proposals including cost analysis, estimate coordination, as well as development and review of trade takeoffs and internal pricing. 
Oversee all capital bids before submission. 
Delegate new customer opportunities within estimating team. 
Evaluate subcontract cost estimates and proposals, as well as preparing/reviewing self-perform estimates, and assembling final estimate for owner. 
Drive and maintain all National Opportunities Reporting. 
Perform productivity analysis of cost estimates, comparisons of scope, quantities, and cost data between projects. 
Negotiate with and engage in subcontract solicitation during the bidding process and maintain master subcontractor/vendor lists by trade. 
Compare and analyze competitive subcontractor and supplier bids. 
Exceed expectations with excellent customer service, operational excellence, and strategic insight. 
Maintain company quality standards with subcontractors and vendors while performing in a high-volume bid environment. 

 Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or related field plus a minimum of 5-7 years of experience performing primary responsibilities listed above.  
Proficient with Outlook, Excel, and Word, along with estimating software. 
Demonstrated experience with heavy civil construction projects, specifically water/wastewater treatment plants and process piping.
Ability to build and maintain a positive working relationship with staff, vendors, and clients. 
Exceptional time management and customer relation skills. 
High attention to detail. 
Ability to assist with writing proposals and reports.

About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.
Job SummaryLoenbro is looking for an experienced heavy equipment operator to join our team. We are looking for experienced people who can operate track hoe, skid steer, telehandler for a variety of construction projects. This position is responsible for operating heavy equipment, preparing job sites, performing basic maintenance on machinery, and ensuring compliance with all safety regulations and guidelines.
Essential Job Responsibilities

Perform daily inspections of equipment to ensure proper functionality and safety.
Perform light maintenance on equipment as required to ensure optimal performance.
Adhere to all safety regulations to ensure a safe and compliant work environment.
Submit daily reports detailing equipment status, work progress, and any issues encountered.
Operate a diverse range of heavy equipment to support project needs and ensure efficient completion of tasks.
Perform all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications
Required:

PEC certificate holders are preferred.
Highschool Diploma or GED required. 3+ years of operating heavy equipment experience required.
Basic mechanical knowledge and skills.

Preferred:

Candidates who have experience with operating an Excavator.
Must be able to clearly explain steps and provide clear directions.
Must be able to complete and complete the paperwork required for purchase orders, time sheets, etc. and answer questions about the construction processes for field staff and other subcontractors.
Must be willing to embrace the company’s core values.

Physical Demands and Work Environment
The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work Environment:

Potential exposure to extreme cold and hot temperatures.
Manufacturing, pipeline, and refining environment.
Fit and move in confined spaces including tanks and vessels.
Limited working surfaces.
Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors.
Exposure to areas with limited visibility.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.
Benefits
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) retirement plan with company match.
Paid time off (PTO).
Life and disability insurance.
Professional development and training opportunities.
Employee assistance program (EAP).

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.
Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities. If you are ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

Living with Integrity
Exceeding Expectations
Acting with Urgency
Delivering Excellence

…we want to hear from you.
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Position Summary
The Foreman is responsible for overseeing and coordinating daily pipeline construction, installation, maintenance, and repair activities. This role provides direct supervision to field crews, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and in compliance with company standards, client requirements, and regulatory guidelines. The Pipeline Foreman serves as the primary field leader and acts as the key liaison between craft personnel, subcontractors, and project management.
Essential Responsibilities

Supervise and direct pipeline construction crews in the installation, maintenance, and repair of pipeline systems.
Plan and coordinate daily work activities, manpower, equipment, and material requirements.
Review project drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and construction schedules.
Conduct daily safety meetings and enforce all company, client, and regulatory safety requirements.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, DOT, environmental, and company policies.
Coordinate excavation, trenching, pipe installation, welding, coating, hydrostatic testing, tie-ins, and restoration activities.
Verify elevations, grades, alignments, and installation requirements are met according to project specifications.
Monitor crew productivity, project progress, and quality standards.
Identify and resolve field issues that could impact project schedules or budgets.
Coordinate with inspectors, utility companies, landowners, subcontractors, and project stakeholders.
Maintain accurate daily reports, production records, timesheets, equipment utilization reports, and safety documentation.
Ensure proper use, maintenance, and accountability of company equipment and tools.
Train and mentor crew members, fostering a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
Assist project management with project planning, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Participate in incident investigations and implement corrective actions when necessary.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED.
5+ years of pipeline construction experience.
2+ years of supervisory or foreman experience leading pipeline crews.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction methods, excavation, trench safety, and utility coordination.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and survey information.
Knowledge of OSHA regulations and industry safety standards.
Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to pass pre-employment and client-required screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with oil & gas, natural gas, water, wastewater, or industrial pipeline projects.
OSHA 30 Certification.
NCCER Foreman Certification.
First Aid/CPR Certification.
Competent Person Trenching and Excavation Certification.
Experience managing subcontractors and multiple work crews.
Knowledge of hydrostatic testing, welding inspection processes, and pipeline integrity requirements.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong leadership and team management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction equipment and methods.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Ability to work effectively with project managers, superintendents, inspectors, clients, and field personnel.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Frequent standing, walking, bending, kneeling, climbing, and lifting up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and travel as project demands require.
Ability to safely access active construction sites and uneven terrain.

Work Environment

Heavy civil and pipeline construction projects.
Exposure to construction equipment, noise, dust, vibration, and changing weather conditions.
Travel between project locations may be required.

Medical, dental, and vision insurance 

401(k) retirement plan with company match 

Paid time off (PTO) 

Life and disability insurance 

Professional development and training opportunities 

Employee assistance program (EAP)
