As a critical member of the Starship team, you will supervise and lead a team of laborers and contractors to support the construction and activation of infrastructure for a variety of projects in Starbase, TX.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Oversee and own the day-to-day site management of a fast-paced, high-impact construction project, including the responsibilities below:

Manage a team dedicated to construction site logistics/operations, including work schedules, project progress, and resource allocation
Plan, implement, and enforce construction site logistics to enable broader project goals and schedule
Manage SpaceX construction assets (trailers, portable restrooms, rental equipment, etc.)
Implement and enforce SpaceX safety policies; drive the safety culture on the jobsite through contractor and internal partners
Coordinate and resolve conflicts in the field for contractors and internal partners on a daily basis
Manage site logistics, including daily deliveries, offloading, inventory, storage, and staging of SpaceX-purchased materials
Be responsible for jobsite cleanliness
Maintain, implement, and iterate SpaceX-provided construction barricades as needed
Maintain jobsite SWPP, and enforce compliance with local, state, and federal regulations
Create, enforce, and iterate on schedules for workers and subcontractors in conjunction with the engineering and project management team
Maintain a daily log for the job site’s operations, reporting to management as necessary

Oversee the procurement and execution of specific construction projects as delegated by the engineering and project management team

Provide budgetary costs based upon the preliminary scope of the project
Gather proposals from contractors; assign contracts upon receipt of all proposals
Develop the final cost and schedule for the sub-project, and implement controls as needed to manage cost, schedule, and scope
Coordinate project implementation and track project status
Coordinate with the end user and facilities team for building operations and maintenance
Manage night shift contractors as the project work requires

Make changes in the operation as necessary to best meet construction deadlines, triage issues to the engineering and project management team as necessary to ensure schedule and quality are adequate
Be responsible for contractor badging process
Help with hands-on skilled trade work when necessary (~10% of the time)

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
3+ years of professional experience in the construction or aerospace industries with experience leading or coordinating a labor force
3+ years of hands-on experience with a trade skill falling in one of the following categories: welding, tubing, vertical building, integration, machining, fabrication, or heavy equipment operation

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Field experience in a technical field or in managing a multi-disciplinary team of contractors/laborers
Previous experience with project management and scheduling software
Basic proficiency with 2D or 3D modeling programs
Knowledge of processes of jurisdictional permitting and/or environmental agencies
Understanding of multiple disciplines such as civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, piping, geotechnical, and surveying
Experience with project management of construction projects, including estimating, cost control, scheduling, and contractor management
Experience reading, reviewing, and approving shop and fabrication drawings
Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while maintaining a high sense of urgency in a high-paced, challenging work environment
Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Availability to work extended hours and weekend as needed—flexibility is required
Ability to travel to different sites, as needed, up to 20% travel
Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting the upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings, and climbing hand-over-hand 
Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain
Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise 
Stand: Up to 10 hours per day 
Sit: Up to 10 hours per day 
Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) between 1 to 2 hours per day 
Overhead reach: Up to 10 hours per day 
Walk: Up to 10 hours per day 
Lift/Carry: Up to ≤ 50 lbs. (unassisted) between 1 to 2 hours per day 
Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 6 hours per day 
Kneel/Crouch: Up to 10 hours per day 
Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day 
Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees for 6 hours or greater per day
Must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description
May be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Experience with plumbing design and operation, including domestic water, wastewater, venting, and storm systems
Experience with critical power infrastructure, including UPS systems, backup generators, and automatic transfer switches

title: Supervisor, Power Generation Fluid Systems
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.SUPERVISOR, POWER GENERATION FLUID SYSTEMS
Starbase is standing up on-site supercomputer power generation. The supervisor of power generation fluid systems will lead technicians fabricating, installing, testing, and commissioning piping and components for natural gas, instrument air, demineralized water, cooling water, aqueous ammonia, and associated valves, pumps, heat exchangers, and instrumentation — from prefab/spool yard through field tie-in. You will take technical direction from engineering and turn it into installed, leak-tight, spec-compliant systems and expected to work side by side with the crew when the work demands it, and to build a team that can eventually cover day and night operations.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Supervise prefab/spool-yard and field fluid-system work, including daily schedules, workflow, and multi-shift handoff
Lead and manage a staff of fluid systems technicians, including hiring input, training, and all performance-management tasks
Organize, assign, and track work so spool fabrication, install, field tie-in, test, and punchlist move cleanly across shifts
Fabricate, install, and personally tie in (and hold the crew to the same standard) fluid system components from P&IDs, isometric drawings, and engineering sketches, including:

Stainless steel, carbon steel, and aluminum piping and tubing, including large-bore
Ball, check, control, and isolation valves
Pumps, strainers, heat exchangers, and dry coolers
Pressure regulators, relief devices, sensors, and gauges

Own plant fluid systems for aeroderivative / industrial gas-turbine power generation, including natural gas fuel, instrument air, demineralized water, cooling water, and 19% aqueous ammonia (SCR) systems
Read and interpret work instructions, P&IDs, data sheets, manuals, and drawings; recommend changes that simplify the build and raise rate without sacrificing quality
Perform and supervise hydrostatic, pneumatic, and leak testing; troubleshoot and repair issues found during activation or production use
Connect and verify instrumentation (pressure transducers, thermocouples, flow, and similar) as required for system checkout
Assess skillsets, identify training needs, and build training so the crew can work natural gas, 19% aqueous ammonia, instrument air, demin, and cooling systems safely
Monitor labor hours and overtime; implement time-management and improvement plans with the staff
Provide data and reporting to support departmental metrics and improvement objectives
Ensure product quality and conformance to specifications, codes, and engineering requirements
Maintain tooling, consumables, and critical-spares inventory
Improve area safety and efficiency through regular auditing and continuous improvement (lockout/tagout, hot work, line break, chemical handling)
Initiate and foster cooperation with millwrights, electrical, engineering, OEM advisors, construction, and datahall operations
Continuously improve processes and crew efficiency, utilization, and productivity

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
5+ years of hands-on experience fabricating, installing, testing, and/or commissioning industrial fluid systems (piping, tubing, valves, pumps, and instrumentation)
2+ years of experience leading a crew, shift, or project (supervisor, lead, or equivalent) in a production, construction, test, or plant environment

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

10+ years of fluid-system fabrication and install in a fast-paced power generation, industrial, or mission-critical facilities environment
Experience tying in pipe (field fit-up and connection of fabricated spools or systems — not supervision-only)
Direct experience on gas-turbine or combined-cycle balance-of-plant systems (fuel gas, demineralized water, condensate/feedwater, cooling water, lube oil, or similar)
Hands-on work with one or more of: natural gas piping, aqueous or anhydrous ammonia systems, demineralized water, high-purity water, or data-center cooling (chilled water, condenser water, dry coolers)
Experience bringing a fluid system from development / first article into repeatable production or commissioned plant operation
Experience with pneumatic/hydraulic system fabrication and high-pressure liquid and gas testing
Ability to read P&IDs, isometric drawings, and OEM manuals and turn them into field work
Familiarity with applicable piping codes and practices (e.g. ASME B31.1 / B31.3), lockout/tagout, and line-break / energy-isolation procedures
Professional experience with calibrated measuring instruments
Experience using heavy equipment (overhead cranes, forklifts, manlifts)
Able to adapt to changing work assignments in a fast-paced environment
Demonstrated ability to hire, train, and retain a high-performing technician crew

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Must be available to work extended hours and weekends, which varies depending on site operational needs; flexibility required
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Data Center Controls Tech, Andrews, Texas
category: data center / critical infrastructure construction and engineering
description:
The Data Center Global Controls team is looking for exceptional individuals to join our Controls organization as a Controls Technician for Service & Construction of the Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) within Amazon data centers. If you are passionate about the Customer Experience, think and act globally and have the ability to contribute to major new innovations in the area of building controls and automation this is the challenge you are looking for! The candidate will possess technical background and experience in installation, troubleshooting, operations and/or maintenance of field sensors, controllers, wiring, networking and programming associated with the industrial controls systems. The candidate may also have relevant experience operating and maintaining mission critical electrical and mechanical systems. A Controls Technician shall be responsible for participating in the installation, testing, troubleshooting and startup of equipment and controls system associated with the BMS and EPMS system deployment in the data centers. A Controls Technician is expected to actively innovate on behalf of their customers in the area of Data Center building automation.

Key job responsibilities
• Primarily work in and support multiple data centers by deploying, servicing, and upgrading BMS and EPMS systems.
• Mentor and train Facilities team members on the operation and control of BMS and EPMS systems.
• Manage small to medium-sized projects and programs.
• Perform point-to-point checkouts between field devices and controllers.
• Perform first-line diagnostics, troubleshooting, and maintenance of programming code and hardware associated with BMS and EPMS in data centers.
• Execute provisioning processes for servers, controllers, industrial PCs, and network configurations, including communication testing between third-party devices and controllers or servers.
• Install, replace, configure, and calibrate sensors.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics and control panel drawings with a basic understanding of closed-loop controls, field sensor scaling, and functions typically performed by industrial controllers.
• Supervise low-voltage electrical contractors performing wiring and installation of field devices in compliance with AWS requirements.
• Provide commissioning and systems-level testing support.
• Create red-lined drawings and documentation of systems.
• Follow change management processes to generate work requests and methods of procedures.
• Participate in factory witness tests at vendor or panel builder facilities.
• Perform root cause analysis during testing and commissioning.
• Ensure personnel on site utilize proper safety methodology.
• Perform service activities including monitoring and reviewing ticketing systems, conducting root cause analysis, and prioritizing tasks.
• Actively manage service agreements including vendor labor scheduling, quality assurance, and financial invoice review.
• Participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying, or moving up to 50 lbs of equipment, and utilize OSHA-standard safety equipment including limited weight-bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools, and personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety harnesses.

title: PMO Project Manager (Data Center Construction)
description:
Who We Are:
Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.
The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.
What We Value:
We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.
Who You Are:
The Project Management Office (PMO) Project Manager (Data Center Construction) is the PMO's embedded project management partner to the Pre-Construction and Construction functions. This is not a traditional construction PM role responsible for replacing the technical ownership of the Pre-Construction or Construction teams. Department leaders and subject matter experts retain ownership and accountability for their work. Instead, the PM provides the cross-functional coordination, structure, visibility, and accountability required to move complex initiatives forward across departmental boundaries. Pre-construction and construction activities inherently depend on multiple teams - including Site Development, Operations, Technology, EHS, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and external partners. The PM ensures those dependencies are identified early, responsibilities are clear, decisions occur at the appropriate time, and work across departments remains aligned to broader project and business priorities. The role gives department leadership a partner who can take complex initiatives and create the structure required to execute them effectively while allowing technical leaders to remain focused on their areas of expertise.
What You’ll Do:

Partner closely with Pre-Construction and Construction leadership to understand priorities, upcoming work, constraints, and cross-functional needs.
Translate complex initiatives into clearly defined workstreams, tasks, milestones, owners, dependencies, and decision points.
Establish and maintain visibility into current and upcoming work through the PMO project management systems and reporting processes.
Identify dependencies between Pre-Construction / Construction and Site Development, Operations, Technology, EHS, Procurement, Finance, Legal, and other functions.
Facilitate the cross-functional meetings required to move work forward, with clear objectives, ownership, decisions, action items, and follow-through.
Connect department heads and functional stakeholders when work has broader organizational impacts or requires decisions across teams.
Identify risks, stalled work, unclear ownership, resource constraints, or competing priorities and drive the appropriate conversations toward resolution.
Escalate material risks and decisions to department leadership, the Head of PMO, or business leadership when appropriate.
Partner with department leadership on prioritization and sequencing when multiple initiatives compete for resources or have interdependent timelines.
Support capacity and resourcing discussions by providing visibility into upcoming work, workload, dependencies, and potential constraints.
Ensure required Procurement, Finance, Legal, and other support-function processes are incorporated into project plans and initiated at the appropriate time.
Improve communication between Pre-Construction / Construction and other departments by ensuring relevant information reaches the appropriate stakeholders and other embedded PMO PMs.
Provide objective facilitation when priorities, ownership, timelines, or expectations conflict across departments.
Track execution against agreed business priorities and provide leadership with clear visibility into progress, risks, decisions, and blockers.
Partner with the Head of PMO and other embedded PMO PMs to consistently apply PMO standards, tools, processes, and reporting practices.

What We’re Looking For:

5+ years of experience in project management, program management, construction, infrastructure, engineering, development, or a related environment.
Experience coordinating complex initiatives involving multiple departments, technical teams, and business stakeholders.
Working knowledge of pre-construction and construction processes sufficient to understand dependencies, sequencing, terminology, and business impacts.
Strong ability to take ambiguous or complex initiatives and create structured execution plans.
Demonstrated ability to facilitate cross-functional teams and create accountability without direct authority.
Strong stakeholder-management skills and ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, functional leaders, and executives.
Strong problem-solving skills with an ability to identify organizational gaps, dependencies, and risks before they affect execution.
Experience with project/work management platforms such as Jira and related collaboration and documentation tools.
Strong written and verbal communication and executive reporting skills.
PMP or equivalent certification preferred.

What We Offer (US):

Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus

Flexible Time Off (i.e. unlimited paid vacation days)
Company paid Holidays (11)
Company paid sick leave
Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
3% 401(k) company contribution
Generous paid Parental Leave
Free virtual coaching and counseling sessions through Ginger
Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry
Free daily snacks in-office
Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.
Apply now and join us on our mission to engineer a new economic paradigm.Galaxy respects diversity and seeks to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and job applicants for employment without regard to actual or perceived age, race, color, creed, religion, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, lactation and related medical conditions), gender identity or gender expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital or partnership or caregiver status, ancestry, national origin, citizenship status, disability, military or veteran status, protected medical condition as defined by applicable state or local law, genetic information or predisposing genetic characteristic, or other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.
We will endeavor to make a reasonable accommodation to the known limitations of a qualified applicant with a disability unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business. If you believe you require such assistance to complete the application process or to participate in an interview, please contact careers@galaxy.com.

description:
At Keeley Companies, we believe in empowering our people and fulfilling career aspirations. Primary Responsibilities:

Assist in the installation and construction of concrete pavements, curbs, and sidewalks following project specifications and design plans.
Lift, carry, and transport construction materials, tools, and equipment weighing over 50 pounds to the work area, ensuring the availability of necessary resources for the project.
Assist in preparation and pouring of concrete mixtures into forms or onto surfaces, ensuring accurate placement and distribution.
Assist in performing repairs on concrete surfaces, including patching, resurfacing, and finishing, to ensure a smooth and uniform appearance.
Strike off with experience straight edge techniques, float and finish concrete.
Support the finishing process by smoothing, leveling, and shaping concrete surfaces using appropriate tools and techniques.
Operate and maneuver small equipment like skid steers, mini excavators, backhoes, rollers, etc., as needed for concrete finishing and related tasks.
Assist in inspecting finished concrete work to ensure it meets project specifications, quality standards, and customer expectations.
Collaborate with construction teams, including contractors, architects, and engineers, to coordinate work and achieve project goals.

High school diploma or Equivalent plus a minimum of two years previous experience as a concrete finisher
Ability to travel a 3-4 hour radius outside of home location

About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach, and every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs, we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps build and maintain the critical infrastructure that supports communities across the nation.
Job Summary
The Civil Superintendent is responsible for the overall planning, coordination, execution, and supervision of civil construction projects, including site development, earthwork, grading, excavation, underground utilities, drainage systems, concrete structures, and related infrastructure. This position provides direct leadership to field personnel, subcontractors, and equipment operators while ensuring projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with project specifications and quality standards.
The Civil Superintendent works closely with Project Managers, clients, engineers, and foremen to coordinate resources, monitor production, and drive project success from mobilization through completion.
Essential Job Responsibilities

Read, interpret, and implement project drawings, specifications, contracts, and civil construction plans.
Direct and supervise daily field operations for civil construction projects.
Coordinate crews, subcontractors, equipment, materials, and vendors to ensure efficient project execution.
Develop, maintain, and manage three-week and six-week look-ahead schedules.
Monitor project production rates and implement corrective actions to maintain schedule and budget objectives.
Lead earthwork, grading, excavation, trenching, underground utility installation, storm drainage, paving preparation, and concrete activities.
Conduct site inspections to verify quality standards, project specifications, and safety requirements are being met.
Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal regulations as well as company safety policies.
Lead daily planning meetings, safety meetings, and toolbox talks.
Collaborate with Project Managers on manpower forecasting, scheduling, procurement, and project reporting.
Support estimating and preconstruction efforts through constructability reviews, production analysis, equipment recommendations, and cost evaluations.
Monitor project costs and productivity while identifying opportunities for improved efficiency.
Train, mentor, and develop foremen, operators, and craft personnel.
Maintain positive relationships with customers, inspectors, utility providers, engineers, and other stakeholders.
Identify and pursue opportunities to expand business relationships and generate future work.
Perform all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications
Required

Minimum 5 years of Superintendent experience managing civil construction projects.
Minimum 8 years of experience in heavy civil, sitework, earthwork, utility, or infrastructure construction.
Proven experience leading multiple crews, subcontractors, and field personnel.
Strong knowledge of grading, excavation, trenching, underground utility installation, stormwater systems, and civil site development.
Experience coordinating heavy equipment including excavators, dozers, graders, loaders, compactors, and related construction equipment.
Ability to read and interpret civil plans, profiles, specifications, and utility drawings.
Working knowledge of civil construction methods, means, and sequencing.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and construction scheduling software.
OSHA 30 certification or equivalent safety training.
Trench Safety and Competent Person certification preferred.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

Preferred

Experience supporting industrial, energy, data center, utility, or large commercial projects.
Knowledge of GPS machine control, survey layouts, and grade control systems.
Experience managing self-perform civil crews.
Bilingual English/Spanish communication skills.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Strong leadership and team-building abilities.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strong organizational and planning skills.
Ability to analyze project risks and implement proactive solutions.
Thorough understanding of construction safety requirements and best practices.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.
Ability to effectively manage project schedules, budgets, and field productivity.

Physical Demands & Work Environment
The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work Environment

Outdoor construction environments.
Exposure to varying weather conditions, including extreme heat and cold.
Active construction sites with heavy equipment and moving machinery.
Exposure to dust, mud, noise levels exceeding 85 decibels, and uneven terrain.
Frequent walking on construction sites.
Ability to enter excavations and trenches when required.
Climbing ladders, embankments, and construction equipment.
Frequent standing, walking, bending, kneeling, and lifting up to 50 pounds.
Operation of company vehicles when required.
Valid driver's license and proof of insurability required. All drivers are subject to DMV background record review.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S) policies.
Benefits
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Paid time off (PTO)
Life and disability insurance
Professional development and training opportunities
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.
Our Core Values (LEAD)
At Loenbro, we are guided by our core values:

Living with Integrity
Exceeding Expectations
Acting with Urgency
Delivering Excellence

If you're ready to join a company committed to building exceptional projects, developing outstanding people, and delivering excellence every day, we want to hear from you.

The Scaffold Foreman is responsible for planning, coordinating, supervising, and inspecting scaffold erection, modification, and dismantling activities while ensuring compliance with all safety regulations, project specifications, and company standards. Supervise and direct scaffold crews in the safe erection, modification, inspection, and dismantling of scaffolding systems.

Identify and correct unsafe conditions, work practices, or equipment deficiencies.

Required

High school diploma or GED preferred.

Strong understanding of OSHA regulations and scaffold safety standards.

Ability to work at heights and in varying weather and environmental conditions.
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

title: Survey Technician
description:
Job Title: Survey Technician
Company: Loenbro, LLCBusiness Unit/Department: South                          Location: Dallas, TXReports to: Lead Survey TechnicianEmployment Type: Full-TimeFLSA Classification: Non-exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.
 
Job Summary
Loenbro is seeking a detail-oriented and motivated Survey Technician to support mission-critical construction projects, including hyperscale data centers, advanced manufacturing facilities, and other complex infrastructure developments. This role is responsible for performing field surveying, layout verification, quality control measurements, and construction staking activities utilizing Trimble survey equipment and software platforms. 
The Survey Technician will work closely with project managers, superintendents, engineers, BIM/VDC teams, and craft professionals to ensure accurate project layout, alignment, and documentation throughout all phases of construction. 
 
Essential Job Responsibilities 

Perform construction staking and layout for foundations, structural steel, equipment pads, underground utilities, roadways, electrical infrastructure, and building components. 

Operate and maintain Trimble total stations, GNSS/GPS receivers, robotic instruments, and data collectors. 

Utilize Trimble Business Center (TBC), Trimble Access, Trimble Siteworks, and other survey software to process and manage field data. 

Interpret engineering drawings, BIM models, civil plans, utility plans, and specifications to establish project control points. 

Verify as-built conditions and perform quality assurance/quality control surveys throughout construction activities. 

Establish and maintain horizontal and vertical control networks on active construction sites. 

Collaborate with project management and field operations teams to identify and resolve layout discrepancies. 

Generate survey reports, field notes, stakeout documentation, and as-built deliverables. 

Assist with reality capture activities utilizing laser scanning, GPS technologies, and drone-based mapping programs when applicable. 

Ensure surveying activities align with project schedules while maintaining the highest levels of accuracy and safety. 

Support construction teams in fast-paced mission-critical environments where schedule adherence and precision directly impact project success. 

 
Minimum Qualifications 

High school diploma or GED required. 

Associate degree in Surveying, Civil Engineering Technology, Construction Management, Geomatics, or related field preferred. 

Minimum 2 years of construction surveying experience required. 

Experience supporting large-scale commercial, industrial, mission-critical, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or data center construction projects preferred. 

Working knowledge of survey principles, coordinate systems, control networks, and construction layout procedures. 

Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and engineering documents. 

Valid driver's license and ability to travel to project sites as required. 

 
Preferred Qualifications 

3+ years of experience with Trimble surveying technologies. 

Proficiency with:  

Trimble Business Center (TBC) 

Trimble Siteworks 

Trimble Access 

Trimble GNSS/GPS Systems 

Robotic Total Stations 

Experience integrating survey data with BIM/VDC workflows and Autodesk platforms. 

Familiarity with data center construction, electrical infrastructure, and mission-critical facilities. 

OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification preferred. 

FAA Part 107 Drone License a plus. 

 
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities 

Strong understanding of construction surveying methods and best practices. 

High attention to detail with exceptional measurement accuracy. 

Ability to work in dynamic, active construction environments. 

Strong mathematical, analytical, and problem-solving abilities. 

Effective communication and collaboration skills. 

Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet aggressive project schedules. 

Demonstrated commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement. 

 
 
Physical Requirements & Work Environment 

Ability to work outdoors in varied weather conditions. 

Frequent standing, walking, climbing, bending, and lifting up to 50 pounds. 

Ability to travel to construction sites nationwide as required. 

Must wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) and comply with all safety regulations. 

Ability to safely navigate active construction sites, including mission-critical and industrial environments. 

 
Benefits 
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team: 

Medical, dental, and vision insurance 

401(k) retirement plan with company match 

Paid time off (PTO)

Life and disability insurance 

Professional development and training opportunities 

Employee assistance program (EAP) 

 
Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked. 
 
Our Core Values 
LEAD with Values: 

Live with Integrity – We do the right thing and do what we say, in every Interaction - and practice stewardship to car for the communities where we live & work.  

Exceed Expectations – We anticipate customer needs, deliver Innovative solutions, and dedicate ourselves to creating outcomes that make a real difference.  

Act with Urgency – We take action, adapt seamlessly, and keep projects moving without compromising quality - because our customers priorities are our priorities.  

Deliver Excellence – We combine our passion for quality, our Industry expertise, and our eye for Innovation to make excellence our standard.  

Guided by core values, grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro maintains and enhances the industrial infrastructure that betters our families, customers, and local communities. 
 
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Construction Project Manager, Warranties (Starbase Development)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.CONSTRUCTION PROJECT MANAGER, WARRANTIES (STARBASE DEVELOPMENT)
The Starbase Development Team is seeking a Construction Project Manager, Warranties to own construction quality assurance and the warranty program for residential and commercial infrastructure in Starbase, TX. This role will own build quality and performance initiatives and serve as the primary liaison between the design, construction, and maintenance teams throughout construction and the project life cycle.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Provide onsite assistance at critical facilities with functional testing as required

3+ years of experience with HVAC, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical systems and control systems

description:
Amazon’s Data Centers are industry leading examples of innovation in design, efficiency, and cost effectiveness. As Pre-Construction managers, we are the nationwide team responsible for planning the construction of the Amazon’s new sites. We are on the forefront of creating and delivering the most innovative products to our customers; and are known for innovating the possibilities of cloud computing.

As a Pre-Construction Manager you will support the development and implementation of a Pre-Construction program execution across the nation over multitude of campuses. This role will serve as the primary liaison between Real Estate, Design Engineering, Due Diligence, and other critical partner teams from initial planning, through design development to provide schedule forecasting, construction budgeting, and constructability guidance. Our goal is to find the candidate with extensive practical construction experience with bidding, contracting, construction documents, industry infrastructure, design, and engineering.


Key job responsibilities
• Foundational knowledge of critical data center equipment (Generators, Uninterruptible Power Supplies, Switchgear, Transformers, Power Feeders & Busduct, Chillers, Plumbing, Fire Detection/Suppression, Air Handling Units, Computer Room Air Handling/Conditioning Units).
• Perform constructability reviews of critical scopes associated with the construction of new data centers building and sites and drive improvements in baseline.
• Perform build phasing evaluations in terms of civil, structural, electrical fields for potential sites.
• Determine and communicate site requirements that could impact schedule, cost, delivery of the work and integration of site with surrounding properties.
• Conduct negotiations with land sellers, developers, general contractors and evaluate bids, proposals, and scoping documents with detail and accuracy.
• Manage GC and other third-party vendors delivering preconstruction services during the design phase.
• Define construction scopes and request for proposals to General Contractors. Review bid summaries, schedules and milestones, pricing, in subcontractor level bid evaluations.
• Support issuance of contracting documents (i.e., Work Orders, Purchase Orders, Work Letters).
• Develop handoff project documentation to Construction Manager partners.
• Collect, evaluate, and share lessons learned to direct teammates, and peers in design, and construction teams to achieve continuous improvement across the entire program.
• Ability to travel 25% of the time.



A day in the life
**Why AWS**
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

*Diverse Experiences*
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

*Work/Life Balance*
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

*Inclusive Team Culture*
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

About the team
AMER Precon within the AMER DCCD org are a nationwide team of diverse set of building and construction experts who excel at constructing the innovative infrastructure that keeps the cloud running and growing. We engage with a wide range of internal partner teams from the outset of new site pursuits through to construction. Daily, we think creatively and act boldly to continuously improve our deliveries. We focus on Bias for Action and Insist on the Highest Standards to Deliver Results and Earn Trust with our stakeholders and customers.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

#DCCD_AMER

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- Experience carrying new design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
- Experience in MS Excel, Word, and Windows Operating Systems
- Experience with power management and power monitoring systems

Preferred Qualifications

- 5+ years of project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure experience
- Knowledge of critical data center equipment
- Knowledge of engineering documentation, electrical diagrams and standard operating procedures
- Knowledge of building codes and regulations including Life Safety, BOCA, NFPA, NEC, or OSHA
- Experience in project management in data centers or comparable critical infrastructure
- Experience in Data Center Engineering Operations, with a deep understanding of electrical and mechanical data center infrastructure
- Experience reading and interpreting construction specifications and drawings for all domains

title: Industrial Maintenance Mechanic
location: Monahans, Texas, United States, Kermit, TX, United States
description:
Headquartered in Austin, TX with operations in Kermit and Monahans, TX, Atlas Sand is the leading provider of frac sand to the Permian Basin. We are proud of what we do – we have state of the art manufacturing facilities, high quality products, outstanding customer service, and exceptional work culture and a commitment to giving back to the community. Atlas was established in 2017 by a team of career oil & gas operators led by Bud Brigham. Since then, we’ve added top industrial sand mining talent and have navigated, grown and innovated our way through the recent ups and downs in the commodity markets. We’re very excited about what we see in front of us, and we think you will be too – so come join the team! 
The Industrial Maintenance Mechanic provides technical support for the safe and efficient operation of terminal and logistics equipment with limited supervision. Duties include but are not limited to maintenance and repair of equipment such as bucket elevators, conveyors, pumps, and control devices. Troubleshoots issues, repairs failures of production and facilities equipment and ensures maximum efficiency and effectiveness of operations. Understands process flow and evaluates ways to increase operating efficiency.
Responsibilities:

Gathers technical information to perform the job
Performs equipment walk around and inspects and adjusts equipment; properly disposes of wastes
Performs equipment repairs, changes out parts, checks the status of equipment availability with site supervisors, and follows procedures to pick up parts and supplies from the warehouse
Responsible for all tasks related to predictive and preventative maintenance programs. Tasks include but are not limited to: repair and maintenance of all machinery and equipment such as bucket elevators, conveyors, compressors, and pumps; repair or replacement of control devices such as switches, photo eyes, proximity sensors, pushbuttons, contactors, motor starters, as needed
Performs work order repairs
Performs light welding and cutting to patch holes in chutes and reduce spillage throughout the system
Coordinates and plans down time efficiently to maximize uptime of production
Understands all equipment in depth from electric motors, gearboxes, conveyors, hydraulics, load out chutes, gas and diesel engines, vehicle and machine repairs, with the ability to trouble shoot, analyze, and make quick responsive repairs without guidance
Able to set up operator welders, drill press, grinder, hand tools and other metal working equipment.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS: 

Ability to work in adverse conditions
Required to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl
Must regularly lift and/or move 75-100 pounds frequently
Ability to work at elevated heights without fear
Open and willing to learn operations of a manlift and a forklift
Have strong VERBAL communication skills
Capable of working a rotating shift, 14 on 7 off rotating between days and nights

Qualifications:

High School Diploma or GED required
Sufficient education to make appropriate arithmetic equations and complete written documentation and records; or an equivalent combination of experience, education and training that provides the desired knowledge, skills and characteristics
Must be able to read and interpret drawings, follow routers, use simple math, and use basic hand held measuring tools
Minimum Three (3) years' experience with hydraulics, pneumatics, mechanics and basic electrical repair
Must have experience in maintaining and repairing processing equipment and heavy equipment
Strong electronics experience with controls and drives
Basic computer skills required to use maintenance software to track and log maintenance costs
Proficiency with Microsoft word and Excel are required
Courses and/or logged hours in the industrial maintenance field are recommended
Knowledge in equipment reliability and preventative maintenance preferred
Prior training and certification in the following areas highly desirable: welding certification, vibration analysis, electrical/mechanical, bearing training, conveyor systems, pumps, fans, screening equipment, and vibrating conveying systems

title: Controls Technician (Starship Launch Pad)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.CONTROLS TECHNICIAN (STARSHIP LAUNCH PAD)
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Read and interpret planning documents, schematics, datasheets/manuals, drawings, blueprints, and engineering sketches
Adjust, repair or replace faulty components of ground hardware, test, and integration equipment
Fabricate and install parts and systems used in launch environments using hand tools, power tools, and test instruments
Connect and verify pressure transducers, thermocouples, and other sensors
Install connectors, connector pins, terminals, and lugs
Complete necessary wiring of the electrical ground support equipment for ground systems
Collaborate with launch engineers to troubleshoot failures and issues derived from launch activities
Lay out, build, test, troubleshoot, repair and modify wiring of electronics racks and junction boxes
Perform maintenance tasks as required in a variety of roles for vehicle integration, pad maintenance, site preventative maintenance, general facilities, and any other general maintenance work as required to maintain an operational launch site

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
1+ years of experience designing, installing, or troubleshooting electrical control systems

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Experience working with any of the following instrumentation: Fluke multimeters, resistance temperature devices (RTDs), thermocouples, strain gages, load cells, displacement transducers, pressure transducers
Ability to install, cut, thread and bend rigid conduit
Experience using power tools in a professional capacity
Experience with electronic system assembly and construction
Working knowledge of programmable logic controller (PLC) Hardware, human machine interface (HMI), and/or graphical user interface (GUI)
Intimate knowledge of electronic test equipment – Multimeters, Process Meters, Oscilloscopes
Experience working at a rocket launch facility and supporting launch campaigns
Basic knowledge of Wheatstone bridge theory, ability to apply Ohm’s law, and an understanding of direct current (DC) electronics
Associate degree in instrumentation, control technology, electrical systems, or another related field
Experience working in corrosive environments and mitigation techniques
Operational knowledge of an oscilloscope, multimeter, soldering wires, connectors
System-level troubleshooting skills and the ability to logically solve instrumentation system problems and determine corrective action
Knowledge of signal conditioning concepts for various types of sensors to include the following: Thermocouple Types K, S, and E; thermal conductive (TC) bonding concepts: resistance weld-on and adhesive bond-on types; TC probes through thermowell sheaths; cold Junction compensation concepts
Experience with the following devices: DC power supplies; DC-DC converters; uninterruptible power supply (UPS) installations; heat shrink tubing, cable harnessing, lacing, and proper strain relief concepts
Working knowledge of transducers, operational amplifiers, and the knowledge of measurement techniques for temperature, pressure, flow, displacement, vibration and the application strain gages are also highly desired. Identify required data, data acquisition plans and test parameters, setting up equipment to conform to these specifications
Working knowledge of multiple bus architectures (PCI/PCIe, PXI/PXIe, GPIB, Serial, USB, etc.) and data communication technologies
Demonstrated capabilities in the development of comprehensive project plans that include all tasks; stage/gate milestones, and reviews necessary to successfully develop and implement solutions
Intermediate skill level using Windows operating systems
Intermediate skill level using Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, OneNote)
Knowledge of data acquisition concepts, hardware, and interfacing (SCXI and PXI-based)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Willing to work extended hours and weekends, as needed
Must be able to work the follow shifts:

1st Shift: Monday – Friday (7:00 AM – 5:30PM) 

Stand: Up to 10 hours per day
Sit: Up to 3 hours per day
Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) between 1 to 2 hours per day
Overhead reach: Up to 10 hours per day
Walk: Up to 10 hours per day
Lift/Carry: Up to ≤ 50 lbs. (unassisted) between 1 to 2 hours per day
Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 10 hours per day
Kneel/Crouch: Up to 10 hours per day
Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day
Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees 6 hours or greater per day
Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description
Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Job Title: Operator Excavator
Company: Loenbro, LLCBusiness Unit/Department: Loenbro – South Region                Location: Afton, TX / On-siteReports to: Operator ForemanEmployment Type: Full-TimeFLSA Classification: Non-Exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.
The UMI Operator Excavator is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of excavators and related heavy equipment in support of underground utility maintenance, inspection, repair, rehabilitation, and construction activities. This position performs excavation, trenching, utility exposure, backfilling, and restoration work while ensuring compliance with project specifications, safety requirements, and company standards. The Operator Excavator works closely with foremen, utility crews, inspectors, and project management personnel to support successful project execution.
 
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Operate excavators of various sizes to perform digging, trenching, grading, utility exposure, and material handling activities.
Safely excavate around existing underground utilities, including water, sewer, storm drain, gas, electrical, and telecommunications systems.
Perform precision excavation work in congested utility corridors and confined work areas.
Support underground maintenance and inspection operations by exposing utilities for inspections, repairs, rehabilitation, and replacement.
Load trucks, move materials, and assist with project site preparation and restoration activities.
Read and interpret utility locates, construction drawings, plans, grade stakes, and work orders.
Ensure proper trench depth, slope, and excavation dimensions are maintained according to project requirements and safety regulations.
Work closely with spotters, laborers, and utility technicians to maintain safe excavation operations.
Conduct pre-operation inspections and daily equipment checks.
Identify and report equipment deficiencies, mechanical issues, and maintenance requirements.
Perform routine equipment maintenance, fueling, lubrication, and cleaning.
Maintain awareness of overhead and underground hazards while operating equipment.
Follow all OSHA, company, and client safety policies and procedures.
Complete daily equipment logs, inspection reports, production reports, and required documentation.
Assist with emergency utility repair and restoration efforts as required.
Support operation of additional equipment when needed to meet project demands.

 
Qualifications
Required

High school diploma or GED.
Minimum 3 years of experience operating excavators in utility, civil construction, or underground infrastructure environments.
Experience excavating around existing underground utilities.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to read utility maps, blueprints, and construction drawings.
Knowledge of excavation safety standards and trenching requirements.
Ability to work safely and productively in active construction environments.

Preferred

Commercial Driver's License (CDL).
OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.
Competent Person for Excavation and Trenching certification.
Utility locating experience.
Experience with GPS machine control systems.
First Aid/CPR certification.
Experience operating additional heavy equipment, including loaders, dozers, graders, skid steers, and backhoes.

 
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong proficiency operating hydraulic excavators of various sizes.
Knowledge of underground utility systems and safe excavation practices.
Ability to interpret utility locates, grade stakes, engineering drawings, and project specifications.
Understanding of trenching and shoring requirements.
Ability to work safely around energized utilities and occupied infrastructure.
Strong situational awareness and hazard recognition skills.
Ability to communicate effectively with crew members and supervisors.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
Basic mechanical aptitude for equipment inspections and minor troubleshooting.

 
Physical Requirements

Ability to sit for extended periods while operating equipment.
Frequent climbing on and off heavy equipment.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds occasionally.
Ability to work around trenches, excavations, uneven terrain, and moving equipment.
Ability to work overtime, weekends, and emergency response assignments when required.

 
Work Environment

Underground utility maintenance and inspection projects
Municipal infrastructure projects
Industrial construction sites
Utility rehabilitation and repair projects
Roadway, right-of-way, and easement work locations
Exposure to dust, noise, vibration, traffic, excavation hazards, and changing weather conditions

 
This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.
 
Benefits
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Paid time off (PTO)
Life and disability insurance
Professional development and training opportunities
Employee assistance program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.
Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities.  If you’re ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

Living with Integrity
Exceeding Expectations
Acting with Urgency
Delivering Excellence

 
…we want to hear from you.
 
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Responsibilities


Responsibilities

Responsibilities:

Budget and Controls 

Monitors the approved project budget, provides oversight, and suggests necessary adjustments for project controls (e.g., Project Expenditure Request (PERs), Professional Services Request (PSRs), Change Orders, Pay Applications, etc.). 

Change Management 

Partners with the Internal Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) and other Microsoft key stakeholders (e.g., Commercial Software Engineering [CSE], and Real Estate & Facilities [RE&F], etc.) and shares updated process flow information with the project team to ensure new processes are being followed that increase program cost savings and improve overall cycle-time and efficiencies. 

Coordination 

Attends and advises during scheduled owner/architect/contractor and other project meetings. 

Drives Results 

Facilitates the delivery of metro-based/campus projects (e.g., new construction and/or retrofits) by making timely data-based decisions in partnership with the local project team and key stakeholders. Champions team and project goals, adhering to business processes, engaging vendor relationships when/where applicable, and fostering positive cross-group collaboration efforts aligned to the program strategy and milestones. 

Financial Acumen 

Creates and applies best practices to identify and incorporate cost-effective solutions for the strategic and tactical delivery of a construction project. Applies influence, strategy, and decision-making to drive solutions, schedules, and manages change with clients, sponsors, and vendors. 

Goal Alignment 

Collaborates and contributes needed technical knowledge to internal teams (e.g., Engineering, Operations, Center for International Social Science Research [CISSR], Commercial Software Engineering [CSE], Legal, Project Controls, etc.) and General Contractors/Subcontractors to maintain the corporate vision and goals for the project. 

Managing Resources 

Oversees timely execution of all procurement activities associated with resourcing and materials necessary for delivering program(s) on time and within project budget forecasts. Evaluates resources and ensures adequate staffing and materials for job completion. 

Project Management 

Drives campus-based delivery solutions (e.g., new or retrofit data center facilities). Analyzes technical information and provides recommendations to support solutions. Assists campus teams in establishing goals for project teams, assigning responsibilities, measuring performance, and seeking and delivering feedback to achieve timely results. 

Project Tracking 

Assists with creating and reporting on project progress regarding scope, schedule, standards, and budge

Risk Mitigation 

Communicates risk mitigation goals and develops metrics, dashboards and/or scorecards to track, communicate, and drive progress. Suggests actions to support organizational and national safety goals.

Advises and monitors the performance of vendors and/or contractors, ensuring compliance with contracts and prior audit results. Reviews vendor performance relative to cash flow and budget summaries (with the cost management team) and clarifies those reports in presentations to the delivery and executive teams. 

Vendor Selection 

Reviews and approves vendor scope of work, design review of site and building plans, pay-application, and invoices.

7+ years of construction program and project management experience in America, including cross coordination amongst disciplines.

title: Site Controller (Construction)
description:
OverviewTract Capital adopts a unique approach to digital infrastructure investment. Leveraging experience and strategic insights honed over three decades of creating successful companies in the space, we excel in nurturing and advancing leading-edge digital infrastructure enterprises. Our team of specialized experts are united by a singular purpose: to support the growth of digital infrastructure. Tract Capital goes beyond simple investment by acting as a strategic partner and catalyst for innovation within the sector. We ensure our engagements not only generate strong financial results but also develop essential digital infrastructure to meet growing demands. Tract Capital has introduced multiple digital infrastructure strategies including horizontal powered land, vertical development, and product development.
 
Position Overview:
Tract Capital is seeking a detail-oriented Site Controller to support active sites in Texas. The Site Controller is responsible for financial oversight of our active data center construction sites. This role ensures rigorous cost governance, proactive financial risk management, and full alignment between Construction, Procurement, Operations, and FP&A. As our data center portfolio grows, this leader will establish scalable financial frameworks and may eventually hire and manage additional Site Controllers.  The right candidate is an inquisitive, data-driven individual who is able to work independently with supporting direction to achieve objectives in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
 
 

 

 

 

 

Job ResponsibilitiesThe successful candidate will be responsible for the following key areas:
 
Full Lifecycle Project Financial Ownership
·       Own the development of financial processes for Data Center construction cost/budget requests through Data Center operations.
·       Build and maintain financials, including customer budgets, forecast updates, total cost of ownership, and monthly cash-flow projections.
·       Establish financial guardrails and enforce compliance across relevant stakeholders, including Design, Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Operations, in collaboration with compliance teams including Supply Chain and Legal.
Financial Transformation: Procore Financial Controls & NetSuite Integration
·       Administer and optimize Procore financial modules, including:
o   Budgets
o   Commitments (POs)
o   Change events
o   Invoices
o   Prime contracts and payment workflows
·       Enable Procore/Financial ERP integration by ensuring flawless 3-way matching across Procore, NetSuite, and vendor invoices.
·       Provide and monitor variance reporting across Procore, NetSuite, and other financial systems, including movement of commitments, contingencies, and retained funds.
Variance Analysis & Forecast Accuracy
·        Conduct monthly, weekly, and ad-hoc financial deep dives for project financial reporting.
·        Analyze PO/invoice deviations against customer and/or internal budgets and create action plans to mitigate risks.
·        Present financial performance to stakeholders, including Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, Supply Chain, Legal, and Finance.
Vendor Reporting Against Internal Budgets
·        Partner with business requestors and Business Owners who manage relationships with relevant vendors during construction and operations to monitor and report against budgets.
·        Coordinate with Procurement on contract negotiation support and vendor financial vetting.
Financial Documentation, Audit & Compliance Excellence
·       Own all financial documentation and audit readiness for each project to ensure compliance with corporate policies and customer requirements, including:
o   Financial documentation to support customer audits, including hard costs and soft costs
o   Approved budgets and revisions
o   Costs/spend against approved budgets, including PO logs and change-event history
o   Vendor documentation against POs
·       Preparation for internal and external audits with complete financial traceability
Financial Reporting & Executive Visibility
·       Deliver highly accurate project financial reporting packages, including:
o   Monthly leadership dashboards
o   Regular project financial reports
o   Financial cash-burn curves
o   Financial scenario modeling
Scaling the Site Control Function
·       Build standards, templates, SOPs, and reporting frameworks for future site controllers.
·       Define org structure and participate in hiring as portfolio grows.
·       Develop best practices for financial governance across all future data centers.
·       Perform additional duties as required to support project delivery and organizational objectives.
 
Education and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA is a plus.
6–10+ years in project finance, cost control, construction accounting, or infrastructure development.
Deep knowledge of Procore Financials and strong ERP proficiency (NetSuite preferred).
Experience with large-capex projects ($1B+ ideal).
Strong modeling, analytical reasoning, and financial operations skills.
Ability to partner with construction leaders and push back tactfully when needed.
Strong documentation, process discipline, and comfort with fast-paced scale environments.

Location: Project site / field-based Austin, TX
Travel Requirement: Limited travel between sites
Expected Salary Range: $160,000 - $200,000 Base Salary + Discretionary Bonus
Tract Capital Employment
Tract Capital employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO.
NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the organization’s ongoing needs.
Tract Capital is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants are considered for employment regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or veteran status. If you need assistance applying for any of our open positions, please contact us at info@tractcapital.com.

·       Build and maintain financials, including customer budgets, forecast updates, total cost of ownership, and monthly cash-flow projections.

·       Establish financial guardrails and enforce compliance across relevant stakeholders, including Design, Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Operations, in collaboration with compliance teams including Supply Chain and Legal.

Financial Transformation: Procore Financial Controls & NetSuite Integration

·       Administer and optimize Procore financial modules, including:

o   Budgets

o   Commitments (POs)

o   Change events

o   Invoices

o   Prime contracts and payment workflows

·       Enable Procore/Financial ERP integration by ensuring flawless 3-way matching across Procore, NetSuite, and vendor invoices.

·       Provide and monitor variance reporting across Procore, NetSuite, and other financial systems, including movement of commitments, contingencies, and retained funds.

Variance Analysis & Forecast Accuracy

·        Conduct monthly, weekly, and ad-hoc financial deep dives for project financial reporting.

·        Analyze PO/invoice deviations against customer and/or internal budgets and create action plans to mitigate risks.

·        Present financial performance to stakeholders, including Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, Supply Chain, Legal, and Finance.

Vendor Reporting Against Internal Budgets

·        Partner with business requestors and Business Owners who manage relationships with relevant vendors during construction and operations to monitor and report against budgets.

·        Coordinate with Procurement on contract negotiation support and vendor financial vetting.

Financial Documentation, Audit & Compliance Excellence

·       Own all financial documentation and audit readiness for each project to ensure compliance with corporate policies and customer requirements, including:

o   Financial documentation to support customer audits, including hard costs and soft costs

o   Approved budgets and revisions

o   Costs/spend against approved budgets, including PO logs and change-event history

o   Vendor documentation against POs

·       Preparation for internal and external audits with complete financial traceability

Financial Reporting & Executive Visibility

·       Deliver highly accurate project financial reporting packages, including:

o   Monthly leadership dashboards

o   Regular project financial reports

o   Financial cash-burn curves

o   Financial scenario modeling

Scaling the Site Control Function

·       Build standards, templates, SOPs, and reporting frameworks for future site controllers.

·       Define org structure and participate in hiring as portfolio grows.

·       Develop best practices for financial governance across all future data centers.

·       Perform additional duties as required to support project delivery and organizational objectives.

 

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA is a plus.
  • 6–10+ years in project finance, cost control, construction accounting, or infrastructure development.
  • Deep knowledge of Procore Financials and strong ERP proficiency (NetSuite preferred).
  • Experience with large-capex projects ($1B+ ideal).
  • Strong modeling, analytical reasoning, and financial operations skills.
  • Ability to partner with construction leaders and push back tactfully when needed.
  • Strong documentation, process discipline, and comfort with fast-paced scale environments.

Location: Project site / field-based Austin, TX

Travel Requirement: Limited travel between sites

Expected Salary Range: $160,000 - $200,000 Base Salary + Discretionary Bonus

Tract Capital employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO.
